header.running_head: Teaching Guests and Those who Came to Madinah

blocks.text:
his legs stretched out. As he approached the gathering, the people made way for him, saying, 'Sit here, O Ashaj.' Rasulullaah ﷺ was now sitting up, holding his legs up. Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'Sit here, O Ashaj.' He sat on Rasulullaah ﷺ's right hand side and, sitting up straight, Rasulullaah ﷺ welcomed him and treated him warmly. Rasulullaah ﷺ then asked him about his land, taking the names of various places in the territory of Hajar, such as Safa and Mushaqar. 'May my parents be sacrificed for you, O Rasulullaah ﷺ!' Mundhir said in astonishment, 'You know the names of our towns better than us.' Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'I have travelled extensively through your land.'
Rasulullaah ﷺ then turned to the Ansaar saying, 'O assembly of Ansaar! Treat your brothers well because together with being Muslims like you, they also resemble you most closely in hair and complexion. (Like you) They have accepted Islaam willingly and have neither been forced to accept nor was there any need to attack and fight them for refusing to accept.' (The Ansaar then hosted the delegation).
Some time later, Rasulullaah ﷺ asked the delegation, 'How did you find the hospitality that your brothers gave you?' They replied, 'They are the best of brothers. They gave us soft beds to sleep in, superb food to eat and they spent their days and nights teaching us the Book of our Rabb and the Sunnah of our Nabi ﷺ.' This impressed Rasulullaah ﷺ and made him very happy. Rasulullaah ﷺ then turned to each one of us to assess what we had learnt and what we had been taught. While some of us had learnt the Tashahhud, some had learnt Surah Faatiha, others had learnt a Surah, others two Surahs and there were also others who had learnt one or two Sunnah practices." The narration still continues further in great detail. [^1]

Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) reports, "We were sitting with Rasulullaah ﷺ when he said, 'A delegation from the Abdul Qais have come.' We could see no one, but after a short while, we saw that they had arrived. After they had greeted Rasulullaah ﷺ, he said to them, 'Have you any dates or any provisions left over?' When they said that they had, Rasulullaah ﷺ had a leather spread laid out. They then poured out the dates they had left over and Rasulullaah ﷺ gathered the Sahabah (RA) around. Rasulullaah ﷺ then said to them, 'This date is called Barni.' He then proceeded to name all the different varieties of dates and the delegation confirmed all the names as correct.
Thereafter, Rasulullaah ﷺ gave instructions for every man of the delegation to be hosted by one of the Muslims, who would teach him the Qur'aan and salaah. They stayed a week, after which Rasulullaah ﷺ summoned them and assessed that they had not yet learnt well enough and had not yet developed a keen understanding (of Islaam). Rasulullaah ﷺ then handed them over to another group of Muslims, with whom they stayed for another week. When Rasulullaah ﷺ again summoned them (and assessed them), he discovered that they had learnt well and developed a sound understanding.
